title: Unauthenticated users can directly access the post-login branch-selection screen by URL
preconditions: Fresh browser session/tab with no prior login and no existing authentication token.
stepsToReproduce: 1. Open a fresh browser context (no cookies/local storage from a prior session).
2. Navigate directly to http://host81.kapilits.com:8007/#/Userbranchselection without logging in.
3. Observe the page that is rendered.
expectedResult: The application should detect the absence of a valid session/auth token and redirect the user back to the Login screen.
actualResult: The Branch Selection screen is rendered directly, showing the 'Select Branch' search UI, an account avatar icon in the header, and a Logout link, without requiring authentication.
evidence: qmetry/evidence/BUG-001_evidence.png (screenshot); Playwright trace retained in test-results/
rootCause: Requires developer/backend investigation. Likely cause (not confirmed): the client-side route guard for #/Userbranchselection does not verify a valid auth token before rendering, or the Angular route resolver fails open when no token is present.
recommendedResolution: Implement/verify a route guard (e.g. Angular CanActivate) on all post-login routes that checks for a valid, server-verified auth token before rendering, and redirect to /Login when absent. Additionally verify equivalent enforcement on backing API endpoints.

title: Primary Contact Number field on the Contact form accepts non-numeric characters
preconditions: Logged in as admin, branch NEYVELI CAO selected, New Contact form open (Individual).
stepsToReproduce: 1. Open Contact > New to load the Individual contact creation form.
2. In the Primary Contact Number field, enter a 10-character alphabetic string, e.g. 'abcdefghij'.
3. Move focus to another field (e.g. Father Name) to trigger field-level validation.
4. Observe whether any validation message appears for the Primary Contact Number field.
testData: Primary Contact Number = 'abcdefghij' (10 letters, no digits); also confirmed with '90000000011' (11 digits) and '+919000000001' (leading plus sign)
expectedResult: The field should be flagged as invalid because it does not contain a plain 10-digit numeric phone number - whether the issue is wrong character class, too many digits, or disallowed symbols.
actualResult: No validation message appears for any of the three cases. The field only enforces a MINIMUM fixed length of 10 characters (confirmed separately: a 3-character numeric value correctly triggers 'Enter the data with minimum(10) fixed length'), but has no numeric-only check and no upper bound: an 11-digit number, a value with a leading '+', and a 10-character alphabetic string are all silently accepted.
evidence: qmetry/evidence/BUG-002_evidence.png (screenshot); Playwright trace retained in test-results/
rootCause: Requires developer/backend investigation. Likely cause (not confirmed): the Primary Contact Number form control only has a minimum-length validator and is missing both a numeric/pattern validator and an exact-length (not just minimum) constraint, e.g. a regex such as ^[0-9]{10}$.
recommendedResolution: Replace the minimum-length-only validator on Primary Contact Number (and Secondary Contact Number) with an exact 10-digit numeric pattern validator (e.g. ^[0-9]{10}$), applied both client-side (Angular reactive form validator) and server-side, and surface a clear 'Contact number must be exactly 10 digits' message.

title: Pincode field on the Contact Address form has no format or length validation
preconditions: Logged in as admin, branch NEYVELI CAO selected, New Contact form open, Address Details tab active.
stepsToReproduce: 1. Open Contact > New, go to the Address Details tab.
2. Enter 'ABCDEF' (non-numeric) in the Pincode field and move focus away - observe no error.
3. Enter '12345' (5 digits) in the Pincode field and move focus away - observe no error.
4. Enter '1234567' (7 digits) in the Pincode field and move focus away - observe no error.
testData: Pincode = 'ABCDEF', '12345', '1234567' (a valid Indian pincode is exactly 6 numeric digits)
expectedResult: The Pincode field should reject non-numeric input and enforce an exact 6-digit length, consistent with Indian postal code format.
actualResult: None of the three invalid values (non-numeric, 5-digit, 7-digit) triggered any validation message. The field appears to have no format or length constraint at all, unlike Primary Contact Number, PAN, and Email which each have at least partial validation.
rootCause: Requires developer/backend investigation. Likely cause (not confirmed): no validator is attached to the pPinCode form control at all (neither pattern nor length).
recommendedResolution: Add a 6-digit numeric pattern validator to the Pincode form control (e.g. ^[0-9]{6}$), client-side and server-side, with a clear 'Enter a valid 6-digit pincode' message.

title: PAN Card No. field accepts lowercase letters despite enforcing the PAN format otherwise
preconditions: Logged in as admin, branch NEYVELI CAO selected, New Contact form open.
stepsToReproduce: 1. Open Contact > New.
2. Enter 'abcde1234f' (valid PAN pattern but lowercase) in the PAN Card No. field.
3. Move focus away and observe whether an 'Invalid PAN Card No.' message appears.
testData: PAN Card No. = 'abcde1234f' (compare: 'ABCDE1234F' is accepted; '1234567890' and 'ABC123' are correctly rejected as 'Invalid PAN Card No.')
expectedResult: Since real PAN numbers are always uppercase, a lowercase entry should either be auto-uppercased or rejected as invalid, consistent with the field's own format enforcement for digit/letter placement.
actualResult: The lowercase value was accepted with no 'Invalid PAN Card No.' message and no auto-uppercase transformation, even though the field does correctly reject a PAN with the wrong digit/letter pattern.
rootCause: Requires developer/backend investigation. Likely cause (not confirmed): the PAN pattern validator regex uses a case-sensitive character class limited to A-Z and does not also test the lowercase equivalent, and no uppercase-transform is applied on input.
recommendedResolution: Either auto-uppercase PAN input as it is typed (common UX pattern also seen on the Name field in this same form) or make the pattern validator case-insensitive and reject lowercase explicitly with a clear message.

title: Primary Email ID format validation does not catch consecutive dots
preconditions: Logged in as admin, branch NEYVELI CAO selected, New Contact form open.
stepsToReproduce: 1. Open Contact > New.
2. Enter 'qa..test@example.com' (consecutive dots before the @) in the Primary Email ID field.
3. Move focus away and observe whether 'Invalid Primary Email ID' appears.
testData: Primary Email ID = 'qa..test@example.com' (compare: 'notanemail', 'qa test@example.com', and 'qa@@example.com' are all correctly rejected)
expectedResult: An email with consecutive dots in the local part is not a valid email address per RFC 5321 and should be rejected like the other malformed variants tested.
actualResult: No 'Invalid Primary Email ID' message appeared; the value was accepted. This is a minor gap in an otherwise mostly-working email regex (missing '@', double '@', and embedded spaces are all correctly caught).
rootCause: Requires developer/backend investigation. Likely cause (not confirmed): the email validation regex does not include a check for consecutive dots in the local part.
recommendedResolution: Low priority - tighten the email validation regex to reject consecutive dots, or adopt a standard RFC 5322-compliant email validator.

title: Save Contact silently fails after using "+ Add" on Address Details or KYC Documents - stale required validators block the whole form with zero user feedback
screen: New Contact - Address Details / KYC Documents (#/configuration/contact)
testCaseId: Manual verification (see Root Cause Analysis below); not covered by an automated TC_CONTACT_* ID
preconditions: Logged in as admin, branch NEYVELI CAO selected, New Contact form open (Individual), all top-level mandatory fields filled in (Title, Name, Father Name, Primary Contact Number).
stepsToReproduce: 1. Fill in the Address Details tab (Plot/Flat No., Street/Building, Area, City/Village, Country, State, District, Pincode) and click '+ Add'. The address correctly appears in the 'Select Primary Address' table below.

2. Open the KYC Documents tab, select Document Type = 'Address Proof', Document Name = 'Aadhar Card', enter a valid-format Reference Number, Month, Year, and upload a file, then click '+ Add'. The document correctly appears in the 'KYC documents and Income Proof' table below.
3. Click 'Save Contact'.

4. Observe: no success message, no error/warning toast, and no network request is sent (confirmed via browser DevTools / Playwright network capture - zero POST calls fire when Save Contact is clicked in this state).

5. Inspect the Address Details and KYC Documents tabs again: the single-entry input fields (Plot/Flat No., Street/Building, Area, City/Village, Pincode, Document Name, Reference Number, etc.) are empty, exactly as left after step 1/2's '+ Add' cleared them.

6. Re-populate those same input fields with the same values again (without clicking '+ Add' again) and click 'Save Contact' immediately: the Address-related fields stop blocking the form (confirmed via Angular's .ng-invalid state disappearing for pAddress1/pAddress2/pAddress3/pCity/pPinCode), demonstrating that re-filling the emptied fields is what was missing.
testData: Any valid contact data; the defect is structural and reproduces regardless of the specific values entered.
expectedResult: After successfully adding an address and a KYC document to their respective lists via '+ Add', the contact record should be created when 'Save Contact' is clicked, since both required pieces of information (address, KYC document) are visibly present in their summary tables. At minimum, if the form is still considered invalid, the user should see a clear message explaining what is missing.
actualResult: Save Contact is a complete no-op: no API call fires, no message is shown, and the button gives no visual feedback that anything went wrong. The user has no way to know why saving 'does nothing'. Root cause traced (see below): the Address Details and KYC Documents sections are implemented as single reactive-form FormGroups whose individual input controls (pAddress1, pAddress2, pAddress3, pCity, pPinCode for Address; pDocumentGroupId, pDocumentId, pDocReferenceno, pDocumentName for KYC) carry Validators.required. Clicking '+ Add' pushes the current values into a separate list/array for display and visually clears the input row, but does NOT remove or relax the required validators on those now-empty controls, and does NOT exclude that FormGroup from the parent Contact form's overall validity calculation. The parent form therefore remains permanently .invalid after any '+ Add' action, and the Save Contact click handler appears to check the parent form's validity before attempting to submit - so it exits early with no submission and no user-facing error, since the code path that would normally render field-level error messages (as seen for the top-level Personal Details / Contact Information fields) is apparently not wired up for this specific silent-exit case.
evidence: Reproduced and confirmed live across 6+ manual verification passes with browser network capture (zero POST requests observed on Save Contact click while stale invalid controls were present); disappeared for the Address fields specifically after re-populating them immediately before Save, confirming the mechanism.
rootCause: Angular reactive-form required validators remain attached to the transient 'add new row' input controls in the Address Details and KYC Documents sections after their values are committed via '+ Add', and those controls are not excluded from (or re-validated out of) the parent Contact form's overall FormGroup validity. Save Contact appears to gate on parent-form validity with no fallback error UI for this specific case, resulting in a silent no-op.
recommendedResolution:
For the dev team - two complementary fixes are recommended:
1. STRUCTURAL FIX (root cause): Move the Address Details and KYC Documents 'add new entry' inputs into their own child FormGroup that is separate from the main Contact FormGroup (e.g. `this.addressEntryForm` / `this.kycEntryForm` rather than nesting `pAddress1` etc. directly under the parent contact form). The parent Save Contact form's validity should be derived from the LENGTH of the committed address/KYC arrays (e.g. `addresses.length > 0`), not from the transient entry-row controls' own validity. This is the standard Angular pattern for 'add to list' UI and will make the bug structurally impossible to reintroduce elsewhere in the app (the same '+ Add' pattern is also used in the Bank Details, Income, and Related Parties tabs, and in the Business Entity form, and should be audited for the same issue).
2. DEFENSIVE FIX (fail loud, not silent): Regardless of the structural fix, the Save Contact button's click handler should never silently no-op. If `contactForm.invalid` is true when Save is clicked, call `markAllAsTouched()` (or equivalent) on the whole form tree and surface a visible summary of which fields/sections are actually invalid, mirroring the existing 'Title Required' / 'Name Required' style toast already used for the top-level fields. This turns any future validator/state bug into a visible, debuggable, user-reportable issue instead of a silent dead end.

title: Save on Group Formation form is blocked by a stale "Chit Period Required" validator even when Chit Period holds a valid, ng-valid selection
preconditions: Logged in as admin, branch NEYVELI CAO selected, Group Formation form open.
stepsToReproduce: 1. Open Group Formation (#/configuration/chitformation).
2. Select a valid Chit Value (e.g. '10,000.00-B') from the dropdown.

3. Select a valid Chit Period (e.g. '12 Months') from the dropdown - confirmed the control's own CSS class list shows 'ng-valid' immediately after selection, i.e. Angular considers this single control valid in isolation.
4. Fill No. of Auctions, a unique Chit Group Code, and Maximum Subscription with valid values.
5. Click 'Save'.
6. Observe the page: 'Chit Period Required' (and, separately, 'Auction Date Required' if the auction date/week toggle was not completed) is shown, and zero non-GET API calls are fired.
testData: Chit Value='B' (10,000.00-B), Chit Period='X1-12' (12 Months), No. of Auctions='12', Chit Group Code=synthetic unique value 'QATESTnnnnnn', Maximum Subscription='1'
expectedResult: Since Chit Period holds a valid selection (confirmed via the control's own ng-valid state), submitting the form should not report 'Chit Period Required'; Save should proceed to call the save API (or report only the fields that are genuinely still empty, e.g. Auction Date).
actualResult: 'Chit Period Required' is shown and Save fires zero API calls, even though the visible/active Chit Period control's own class list is 'ng-valid ng-dirty ng-untouched' at the moment of submission. This is the same class of defect as BUG-006 on the Contact form: a required-field check that does not agree with the individual control's own validity state, resulting in a silent block with no way for the user to know Chit Period is the (apparently mistaken) blocker.
evidence: Reproduced via Playwright with live DOM class inspection immediately before Save click, confirming Chit Period's own control was ng-valid while the page-level message still read 'Chit Period Required' and zero API calls were observed.
rootCause: Requires developer/backend investigation. Likely cause (not confirmed, but consistent with BUG-006's pattern in this codebase): the Group Formation page renders more than one instance of the Chit Period control in the DOM (a duplicate-hidden-component pattern already observed on the Contact Detail/Employee role forms), and the submit-time required check may be reading a different (stale/hidden) FormControl instance than the one the user actually interacted with, or the parent form's cross-field validator recomputes validity from a source that is not kept in sync with the visible control.
recommendedResolution: For the dev team: 1) Audit the Group Formation component for duplicate/hidden instances of the Chit Period (and other) form controls, consistent with the pattern already flagged in BUG-006 for the Contact module - ensure only one FormControl instance backs each visible field. 2) Verify the Save click handler's required-field check reads validity from the same FormGroup instance that data-binds to the visible dropdown, not a stale or duplicate one. 3) As a defensive fix, never let Save silently no-op with zero API calls - call markAllAsTouched() and render a visible, field-specific error summary so a genuine validator/state mismatch is immediately visible and reportable rather than appearing as 'nothing happens'.
